name: Steering and Controls
description: Steering is turning redstone and rotation into thrust and angles.

pages.title: Steering and Controls
pages.text:
[#](FFFFFF)[#]() **Key points**

- [#](FFFFFF)[#]() Steering turns redstone and rotation into thrust and angles.
- **Steering Wheel**: hold right-click and move the mouse. **Throttle Lever**: right-click and drag.
- **Aeroworks consoles**: right-click empty-handed to take control; Esc lets go.
Steering is turning redstone and rotation into thrust and angles. Simulated supplies wheels, levers and sensors. Aeroworks adds control consoles and servos.

pages.title: Steering Wheel
pages.text: Hold right-click and move the mouse to turn. It stays at the angle you leave it. Sneak snaps to 45 degrees, and its panel sets the most it turns either way. A comparator at its back reads whether it is held; one against each side lights only while it is turned one way.

pages.title: One wheel
pages.text:
Steer with one wheel, not a lever per side:

- Its cog turns a [#](2E5AAC)[Swivel Bearing](entry://flight/ship_building)[#]() under a stern propeller.
- Or a comparator at each side of it slows one side's propeller line through an Analog Transmission; Redstone Links reach pods.

Levers are for settings.

pages.title: Throttle Lever
pages.text: A compact analog redstone source: right-click and drag. A [#](2E5AAC)[wrench](entry://create_basics/tools_wrench)[#]() inverts the signal.

pages.title: Analog Transmission
pages.text: Unpowered, its cogwheel turns with its shaft. A redstone signal slows the cogwheel to (15 - signal)/16 of the shaft's speed, and 15 stops it. The shaft runs through at full speed.

pages.title: One throttle
pages.text:
One Throttle Lever sets the speed:

- An Analog Transmission in each propeller line: shaft from the engine, cogwheel toward the propeller.
- Wrench the lever once: pulled back stops them, pushed forward is flat out.
- Links carry its strength to pods.

pages.title: Navigation Table
pages.text: Outputs redstone toward a destination, weaker when you are not facing it. Different Navigation Items give different targets.

pages.title: Sensors
pages.text:
The sensors give redstone signals:

- **Altitude, Velocity and Gimbal Sensors**: from height, speed and tilt.
- **Laser Pointers, Laser Sensors and Optical Sensors**: detect objects.
- **Modulating and Directional Linked Receivers**: read distance or angle to [#](2E5AAC)[Redstone Links](entry://create_basics/redstone_and_control)[#]().

pages.title: Aeroworks consoles
pages.text:
Aeroworks consoles hold modules: Yoke, Joystick, Throttle Quadrant, Pedal, Lever, Wheel and buttons.

- **Sneak-right-click** to bind keys and [#](7A3C9A)[Redstone Link frequencies](entry://glossary/redstone_frequency)[#]().
- **Right-click empty-handed** to take control; Esc lets go.
- Touching consoles join into one deck.

pages.title: Control Desk
pages.text: Mount modules in its sockets, and use a wrench to remove them. They keep their settings. Styles change with materials.

pages.title: Mechanical Servo
pages.text: Turns a redstone strength into an angle within a set range. Stepper Servos move in fixed steps, either direction.

pages.title: Aeroworks Gyroscope
pages.text: Helps hold a ship level. It needs rotation: full strength at 256 RPM, drawing 16 su per RPM. Without rotation it does nothing. Hover over it for its status and stability.
